label: June 8–14
title: “The Lord Looketh on the Heart” —  1 Samuel 8–10; 13; 15

items.text: The Lord sees past our labels, our physical appearance, and our insecurities. He looks instead, 'on the heart.' Even when our heart isn’t quite right, if we are willing, He will give us 'another heart.'

When the Israelites asked for an earthly king, they were essentially rejecting the Lord’s reign over them. We can consider who we look to for safety and guidance and what it means to truly let the Lord ‘reign over’ us.

Unlike earthly kings, Jesus Christ is perfect, eternal, and always mindful of our needs. We can identify worldly influences that might keep us from letting Christ be our King and remove them from our lives.
God calls people by prophecy to serve in His kingdom, just as He chose Israel’s kings. We can learn from the words and actions of those called, those extending the call, and those being served.

Saul's rebellion and stubbornness, despite his initial timidity, demonstrate how pride can lead to downfall. His choices in 1 Samuel 13 and 15 show the danger of prioritizing seemingly good reasons over direct obedience to the Lord.

The principle 'to obey is better than sacrifice' is a vital lesson. We are blessed when we put the Lord’s will first, understanding that obedience to His commandments is always more important than any earthly substitute.

When Samuel looked for a new king, the Lord taught him to look 'on the heart,' not just the outward appearance. We should strive to judge others as the Lord does, seeing their inner worth and potential.

Saul, a keeper of donkeys, was 'little in his own sight' and self-conscious. Yet, he was chosen. This reminds us that the Lord can use anyone, regardless of their perceived status or insecurities, to accomplish His purposes.

David, a shepherd boy, was overlooked by his own family. His faith and courage to defeat a giant demonstrate that true strength and leadership come from the Lord, not outward appearance or social standing.

The Lord’s perspective is eternal and perfect. He sees our potential and our willingness to follow Him, even when we feel inadequate. Trusting in Him allows Him to transform our hearts and guide our lives.
